promise: Additional park land needed (all types)
reported_2026: Since 2017, Metro Parks has acquired 568.78 new acres of land. (Verify: pending Plan to Play 2026 Appendix pages A-474 to A-478.)
notes: 568.78 is the Appendix figure (June 2026 snapshot). Verify: pending Plan to Play 2026 Appendix pages A-474 to A-478 (SOL-055). Later evidence: about 300 acres next to Beaman Park announced July 24, 2026 (Commitments 1353) and a Park Board transfer request for approximately 298.20 acres on September 1, 2026 (Commitments 1357); transfer pending closing, no deed or acceptance record found. If it closes, 568.78 + 298.20 = 866.98 acres. The 309-acre figure on A-478 is a superseded June estimate (SOL-011). Deadline is 2026, so not yet due as of 2026-10-24. 2026 Update p12 restates the target as 4,540; Appendix as 4,500+.

Metro allocations divided by estimated market value: 12,800,000 / 534,362,411 = 2.4%. Appendix A-496 prints 2.2% (source-reported, unverified). $12.8M: Verify, pending Appendix A-474 to A-478. Horizon is 2027, not yet due (SOL-001, SOL-003, SOL-029, SOL-055). Excludes private donations and grants.

promise: NR 1.1 #210: Strengthen hillside development regulations to minimize development on greater than 15% slopes.
reported_2026: Residential grading and clearing limits still start at 20% slopes; lots under one acre preserve slopes of 25% or more; lots of one acre or more are exempt. Three amendments since 2015 (BL2015-1153, BL2019-111, BL2022-1121); none lowers the residential threshold to 15%.
notes: Near term: begin work within 1 to 3 years of 2015 adoption (Vol IV p4), a start window, not a completion deadline; Metro Planning. The code read on 2026-10-22 has no 15% residential threshold, and no Metro document reports status on the action, so no lateness verdict is given (SOL-004). BL2015-1153 added alternative (-A) district names; BL2019-111 added no-STRP (-NS) district names; BL2022-1121 sent subdivisions on 20%+ slopes to Conservation Development (MPC minutes 2022-04-28 p18). The 15% figure applies only to ISR adjustments for multifamily or nonresidential development (Tables 17.28.030A and B), which predate 2015. Code read on Municode 2026-10-22.

promise: NR 1.4 #182: Enact a conservation subdivision ordinance by right with a minimum of 50% open space requirement.
due: Start window: begin by 2021 (table, 4-6 years) or 2022 (Vol IV p4, 4 to 7 years)
reported_2026: BL2022-1121 (Council third reading May 17, 2022) replaced the Cluster Lot Option with Conservation Development: required on R and RS subdivisions where at least 10% of the site has listed natural features, with a 20% preservation threshold.
notes: Mid term printed 4-6 years (Vol IV p4 defines 4 to 7 years), a window to begin work, not a completion deadline. Assessed on the tool enacted, not on lateness: it is required, not by right, and sets 20% rather than 50% (50% requested and 20% enacted are separate standards, not a percentage delivered) (SOL-005, SOL-019). Same ask as pair 13 (2011, due 2012). Related #174 (cluster lots to 33% preserved land): the Cluster Lot Option was removed from the code in 2022 (Metro Planning, Compact Development open house page). BL2006-1046 had defined a 50% conservation subdivision and was withdrawn in 2007. SOL2-2026-11-02: NashvilleNext Vol IV timeframes are start windows, not completion deadlines; no lateness verdict on the conservation-subdivision tool alone.

promise: NR 1.4 #201: Create a street tree policy, residential tree ordinance, maintenance program, and preservation policy; implement and regularly update the Urban Forestry and Landscape Plan.
reported_2026: BL2022-1122 (2022) created Metro Code 17.28.065: an intent to minimize tree removal, tree density of 14 units per acre for new single and two-family subdivisions, and street-frontage trees on new lots. Amended by BL2024-687 (2025).
notes: Near term: begin work within 1 to 3 years of 2015 (Vol IV p4), a start window, not a completion deadline; rules enacted 2022 (SOL-006). The rules apply when land is developed; they set density with retained or planted trees and say "minimize", so they do not stop clearing of existing forest. Rural AG and AR2a lots are exempt from the frontage rule. The Urban Forestry and Landscape Plan (2016) has not been updated in any document here. Street tree policy and maintenance program not assessed.

promise: BE 1.1 / NR 4.2 #323: Update areas to new Rural Community Character Manual policies that guide a reduction in development and discourage the expansion of sewer infrastructure.
reported_2026: Joelton community plan, amended August 24, 2017, applies T2 Rural Countryside to southeast Joelton and T2 Rural Maintenance to most of the rest.
notes: Policy mapping done on time for Joelton (2017). The Planning Commission adopted Rural Character Subdivision Regulations on April 28, 2016 (RS2016-104, 9-0) and the Whites Creek rural policies on May 26, 2016 (RS2016-142, 6-2-2), after deferring them from the June 22, 2015 NashvilleNext adoption (WHITES-CREEK-HEARINGS.md). No document reports whether sewer extensions into T2 areas were limited, which is the outcome the action names. The Bordeaux-Whites Creek plan (p23) says that as of August 2017 the new rural policies "have only been applied within the Whites Creek study area", with more rural areas to follow "as community plan policy areas are updated in the future" (no date). So in 2017 the new policies covered one study area, not all rural land. The Joelton plan of the same date applies Rural Countryside to southeast Joelton; [ASSUMED] that area lies inside the Whites Creek study area. The Bellevue plan does not apply them. The timeframe is a start window, not a completion deadline (SOL-007).

promise: NR 1.2 #119: Research methods to define and identify ecologically valuable lands, and recommend an in-lieu fee to fund a land bank where permanent protection cannot be accomplished.
reported_2026: Ecological Conservation Strategy launched March 2026, expected fall 2027. No in-lieu fee or land bank for ecologically valuable land found.
notes: Long term: begin work within 7 to 10 years of 2015 (Vol IV p4), a start window, not a completion deadline. The action asks Metro to research methods and recommend an in-lieu fee, not to enact one. The strategy may define ecologically valuable land; whether research began earlier is not established, so no lateness verdict (SOL-008); Metro itself calls it the first countywide ecological plan since 2011. The tree bank (tree replacement fees) and the Conservation Assistance Grant Fund are different tools. Searches found no land bank; a records request would settle it.

promise: NR 4.1 #148: Identify risks to upstream landscapes and contribute to joint regional efforts to mitigate them with land conservation, source water protection, hazard reduction and floodplain management.
due: Start window: begin by 2021 (table, 4-6 years) or 2022 (Vol IV p4, 4 to 7 years)
reported_2026: No joint regional land conservation effort for upstream watersheds found in any document here or in web searches.
notes: Mid term (table 4-6 years; Vol IV p4, 4 to 7), a window to begin work. The named implementers are regional partners (Cumberland Region Tomorrow, Nashville Area MPO, Cumberland River Compact, TDEC, adjacent counties), with no Metro department, and the action also covers source water protection, hazard reduction and floodplain management; not a test of Metro alone (SOL-009, SOL-020). A negative finding from searches, not proof of absence.

promise: Stop net tree-loss by 2020.
reported_2026: Davidson County lost just over 900 acres of canopy from 2016 to 2021 (-0.3%). The Urban Services District lost 1,841 acres; the rural General Services District gained.
notes: Draft recommendation: Livable Nashville 2017 is a DRAFT, never adopted, and Sources marks it not counted. The 2016-2021 net change straddles 2020, so it cannot show whether net loss stopped by 2020; a matching adopted target and post-2020 measurements are needed (SOL-018). pct_delivered left blank because the target is zero. Net loss fell in the urban district while rural canopy grew.

pair: Each recommendation and each 2026 status is a row in Commitments (doc + page). pct_delivered is a formula (delivered_value / promised_value), used only where both measure the same thing. Assessment values: Met, Partly met, Not met, Not yet due, Goal restated (the 2026 documents change the baseline or goal), No status reported (no 2026 document reports against the recommendation), Not verified (the delivery evidence does not answer the recommendation). NashvilleNext Vol IV timeframes are windows to begin work (Vol IV p4), not completion deadlines; due shows them as start windows.
